headline: Two multi-agent frameworks running in the same process can both spawn code-executing agents — high conflict if pointed at one workspace.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Either framework's agents can ingest the other's output if the developer wires them together. AutoGen's GroupChat and CrewAI's role chats both treat agent messages as authoritative input. With shared filesystem, file-mediated injection is plausible.
mitigations: Add a verification step between agent handoffs
Sanitize any tool result before passing across frameworks

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both are libraries that call whichever model provider the developer configures. Data leakage is whatever the developer's model choices imply; nothing inherent to either framework leaks more than the other.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both can run code executors with filesystem write. If both are configured to use the same working directory (a likely default), concurrent writes will corrupt outputs. Neither provides cross-framework locking.
mitigations: Use AutoGen's DockerCommandLineCodeExecutor for AutoGen agents and a separate working directory for CrewAI tools
Avoid sharing the same working directory between frameworks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent-to-agent message passing without verification gates is the norm in both frameworks; chained hallucinations are a known failure mode in multi-agent systems.

E_compliance.rationale: Both inherit model-provider terms; equivalent posture if same models used.
